title: Connection saturation, and why pooling beats raising the limit

videos.script: The site is busy, and the database starts refusing connections. Too many clients already. {{error}} The obvious fix is one line of configuration. Raise the limit from a hundred to five hundred, restart, and the errors stop. {{limit}} This lesson measures why that fix makes things worse. {{why}} In PostgreSQL every connection is a whole process, with its own memory. And the server has four processors, however many processes ask for them. {{process}} You run lesson 2's workload at one client, then four, then up to ninety. Throughput stops growing at four. Latency keeps climbing all the way. {{curve}} Then you put PgBouncer in front of the server. Two hundred clients connect to it, and the server sees eight. {{pool}} You meet the price of transaction pooling: a setting one client made, turning up in another client's session. And the prepared statements that break, and the setting that fixes them. {{traps}} Finally you size the pool from a measurement, not from a rule of thumb. {{sizing}}
